text:
Marie L: Heads-up — I'm seeing a spike in spot/preemptible interruptions in us-west1 this morning. Impacting some Dedicated fallback jobs. Can we review alert thresholds and the fallback behaviour? :eyes:
Ben S: Saw it too. Grafana shows interruption_rate over the last 10m ~1.8% (baseline ~0.6%). Link: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/spot/interruptions-us-west1
Carlos M: The pattern looks like a short burst every ~6h that causes retries to pile up for small-batch inference. We hit throttles and push more pods, which just increases pressure.
Emily (cloudops): ops-bot already fired this morning: "spot-monitor:us-west1 interruption_rate>1% (10m)". I've muted noisy alerts but we need a proper long-term change.
Dana P: Proposal: add a mid-priority alert for 5m interruption_rate > 1% with an automated runbook that: (1) scales up mixed-capacity pool (on-demand burst) for 10m, (2) flips fallback to a warm quantized variant, (3) triggers a throttling backoff on retries.
Ben S: Agree. Also suggest we push a short cooldown on autoscaler to avoid reactive overshoot. Right now HPA responds in 30s which is too fast for transient spot blips.
Marie L: Can someone sketch the new Prometheus rule and the action plan? Keep noise low — don't want to spam pg-alerts.
Carlos M: Draft rule (untested):
```
- alert: SpotInterruptionBurst
  expr: increase(spot_interruption_total{region="us-west1"}[5m]) / increase(spot_request_total{region="us-west1"}[5m]) > 0.01
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "Spot interruption rate >1% (5m) in us-west1"
    runbook: "https://wiki.redwood/ops/spot-interruptions"
```
Ben S: Change severity to "high" for 5m sustained, and create a separate "warning" rule for a 15m window at 0.6% to detect ramps. Also add a suppression on known maintenance windows.
Emily (cloudops): Runbook actions we should automate:
- toggle-mixed-pool --region us-west1 --size +10
- update-runtime-config --fallback quantized-warm
- pause-autoscaler-cooldown --duration 10m
ops-bot: Automated check: current mixed-pool available capacity = 0. Will not auto-burst without override.
Dana P: That ops-bot line explains the problem — we don't auto-burst because billing guard is blocking. We should add a policy that allows 10% emergency on-demand burst when interruption_rate>1% for 5m and SLO impact >0.5%.
Marie L: Quick SLO impact check — Carlos, can you add a short eval that correlates 5m interruption spikes to p99 latency regressions for the model-serving routes? If p99 increases >200ms then allow emergency burst.
Carlos M: On it. I'll add a short dashboard panel and a Prometheus recording rule. Will run a dry-run for 24h.
Ben S: Also add a synthetic canary that creates a few small inference requests when the alert fires to verify fallback latency. If canary fails, escalate to page.
Emily (cloudops): I'll own the alert rollout and suppression rules. Plan: test in staging w/ fault-injection tomorrow at 09:00 PT, then prod rollout with 2-hour monitoring window.
Marie L: Awesome. For the message templates, use concise copy: what fired, suggested action (auto-burst on/off), owner, link to dashboard, runbook. Keep pg-alerts minimal.
ops-bot: Note: scheduled maintenance window in us-west1 tomorrow 10:00-11:00 PT — alerts will be auto-suppressed per current policy.
Dana P: After staging validation, we'll commit the Prom rule and the autoscaler cooldown change. Also add a metric for "mixed_pool_burst_count" to track how often we use emergency burst (cost center).
Ben S: +1. One more ask — include cost guard: if emergency bursts >3/day for a week, create a ticket for capacity purchase or model-routing adjustments.
Marie L: Thanks everyone. Action items: Carlos: add eval & dashboard (ETA 6h). Emily: schedule staging test + manage rollout (ETA tomorrow 09:00). Ben/Dana: draft the Prom rules + autoscaler policy (ETA EOD). I'll follow up after the staging run. :thumbsup:
